Certified type:
- Category: Water meter (the schema examples say "Gas meter", so "Water meter")
- Type designations: MUT7000, M10
- Module designation: Not applicable? Not stated — omit or null. Actually schema says module_designation: "Analog load cell" | "Not applicable" | null. This cert doesn't mention modules. Omit (don't fabricate).
- Description: An electromagnetic water meter

Model family: The cert covers 4 meter sizes: DN50/2", DN80/3", DN100/4", DN150/6". Family name: null (or "family of instruments"? The doc says "Table 2 the characteristics of the family of instruments" — family name isn't explicit. Use null.)

Models: DN50/2", DN80/3", DN100/4", DN150/6" — maybe simplify IDs: "DN50", "DN80", "DN100", "DN150". The Table 4 uses "DN50", "DN80; DN100; DN150". I'll use "DN50", "DN80", "DN100", "DN150" for consistency, with labels DN50/2" etc.

Characteristics type_level:
- measuring_principle: "Electromagnetic" (string value)
- accuracy_class: 2 (dimensionless) — value: "2" or number 2? Accuracy class 2 is a class designation; number is fine. I'll use value: 2, unit null.
- environmental_class: "M1 / O (installed outdoors)" — value string "M1 / O", maybe with note. Keep "M1 / O (installed outdoors)" as string.
- electromagnetic_environment: "E1"
- temperature_range_ambient: {min: -25, max: 55}, unit °C
- water_temperature_class: "T50" with range +0.1 to +50 °C. Could record as water_temperature_class: "T50" and water_temperature_range: {min: 0.1, max: 50} °C. The table says "T50 (+0,1 °C / +50 °C)". Convert comma decimals: 0,1 → 0.1.
- maximum_admissible_pressure: 1.6 MPa (16 bar). Record max_admissible_pressure: value 1.6, unit "MPa". Maybe also as bar alternative. I'll record MAP as 1.6 MPa and add max_admissible_pressure_bar: 16? Better: one characteristic "maximum_admissible_pressure" value 1.6 unit MPa, and another "maximum_admissible_pressure" unit bar... Schema allows one value per label at type_level. I could record max_admissible_pressure with unit MPa value 1.6, and add map_alternative? Simpler: record two entries? Keys must be unique. I'll do "maximum_admissible_pressure": value 1.6, unit MPa, and mention 16 bar maybe as separate characteristic "maximum_admissible_pressure_bar": 16? Hmm. Cleaner: max_admissible_pressure: {value: 1.6, unit "MPa"}; also "maximum_admissible_pressure_bar" could be noisy. I'll include both? The rules say don't fabricate but conversion 16 bar is in the source text ("1,6 MPa (16 bar)"). I'll include max_admissible_pressure with MPa, and a second entry "maximum_admissible_pressure_alternative" — too noisy. Just include the MPa one. Actually maybe include both under matrix? No. I'll do one: maximum_admissible_pressure: 1.6 MPa. Perhaps also record bar in a single value object? Value must be number/range/string. Could do value: "1.6 MPa (16 bar)" as string but rules prefer numeric+unit. I'll record max_admissible_pressure: 1.6 MPa and skip bar, or record pressure_loss_class too.

- orientation: "All positions (Horizontal, vertical or diagonal)" — string.
- flow_profile_sensitivity_class: "U0 and D0 (0 x DN upstream and 0 x DN downstream)" — string value "U0 / D0".
- reverse_flow: descriptive string. Could include as description rather than characteristic. I'll include reverse_flow_capability: "designed to measure reverse flow; recorded on separate volume totalization; separate pulse output" — maybe just value string "supported". Hmm, keep it minimal: "reverse_flow_measuring": {value: true}? Rule: value number|string. true is boolean — schema says number|min/max|string. I'll use string "supported" or include full description. I'll record reverse_flow with a short string: "Measured; recorded on separate totalizer with separate pulse output".
- pressure_loss_class: "Δp 16" with value 0.16 bar. Record pressure_loss_class: value "Δp 16" and max_pressure_loss: 0.16 bar. I'll do pressure_loss_class: "Δp 16" and pressure_loss: {value: 0.16, unit: "bar"}.
- power supply: battery 3.6 V (operating range 2.9–3.7 V); DC mains 10.8–13.2 V. Split:
  - power_supply_type: "replaceable battery or DC mains"
  - battery_voltage_nominal: 3.6 V
  - battery_voltage_operating_range: {min: 2.9, max: 3.7} V
  - dc_mains_voltage_range: {min: 10.8, max: 13.2} V

Model_level characteristics from Table 3:
- diameter_inlet_outlet (mm): DN50: 50; DN80: 80; DN100: 100; DN150: 150
- minimum_flow_q1 (m³/h): 0.1, 0.25, 0.4, 1.0
- transitional_flow_q2: 0.16, 0.4, 0.64, 1.6
- permanent_flow_q3: 40, 100, 160, 400
- overload_flow_q4: 50, 125, 200, 500
- ratio_q3_q1: 400 for all — it's constant; could be type_level: 400. Since constant across models, put at type_level. But it comes from model table... Either is acceptable. I'll put ratio_q3_q1 at type_level since it's the same for all models. Hmm, or keep in model_level matrix. The rule: varying attributes in model_level; constant ones can be type_level. I'll put q3_q1_ratio: 400 at type_level.

Table 4 (indicating device):
- indicating_range_minimum_value (m³): DN50: 99999.9999; DN80/DN100/DN150: 999999.999 — varies by model → model_level.
- verification_scale_interval (m³): DN50: 0.0001; others: 0.001 — model_level.

Matrix_tables:
- Table 3: "General characteristics of the family of instruments" with columns meter_size, diameter_in_outlet_mm, q1, q2, q3, q4, ratio_q3_q1.
- Table 4: "General characteristics of the indicating device" — also a matrix; include as matrix_table.
- Table 2 software identification — matrix table with software component rows. Could also record components[] with role bootloader and firmware, type_designations being versions. Components section: role "Bootloader", type versions 1.06, 1.07 with CRC; role "Legally relevant firmware", versions 1.08, 2.06. Hmm, components are physical sub-assemblies; software components might fit better in matrix_tables. I'll add Table 2 as matrix_table with rows for each (identification, software_version, crc_checksum). Also maybe components for software? The schema says components "include ONLY if cert names sub-assemblies". Software is arguably a sub-assembly but I think matrix table suffices. I'll include the software as matrix_table only.

Recommendation:
- id: "R49" (canonical). Edition: 49-1? The recommendation is "R 49-1: 2013". Hmm. The canonical id examples: "R60". Here it's R49-1. id: "R49-1"? The schema says id canonical e.g. "R60" not "OIML R 60". Part designation... I'll use "R49-1" with edition 2013? Edition (int) — 2013 is the year, likely edition. For R60 it'd be edition like 2000 (year). So edition: 2013. Actually "R 49-1: 2013" — the edition is 2013. But part "-1". I'll set id: "R49-1", edition: 2013. Hmm, alternatively id "R49" with edition 2013 and part noted... Schema has no part field. I'll use id "R49-1". Wait — canonical format example converts "OIML R 60" → "R60". For R49-1, "OIML R 49-1: 2013" → "R49-1". I'll go with id "R49-1", edition 2013.
- accuracy_classes: ["2"] — class 2 for water meters. Accuracy class 2 → ["2"].

Test reports:
- NMi-2652375-01, 24 May 2022, 29 pages, role: type_evaluation_report (it's the OIML Type Evaluation Report referenced). Actually page 1 says "represented by the sample(s) identified in the OIML Type Evaluation Report". Page 2 lists the reports. Both could be type evaluation reports. Roles: I'll set both as "type_evaluation_report"? Or first one type_evaluation_report, second test_report? The text: "The conformity was established by the results of tests and examinations provided in the associated report(s)". Both are associated reports. I'll mark both as "test_report"? Hmm. Given the reference to "OIML Type Evaluation Report" singular, likely both together constitute it. I'll set both role "type_evaluation_report". Actually safer: first "type_evaluation_report" (2022, initial evaluation) and second "test_report" (2026, addition of DN50/DN150 and software update — extension). That's an inference. I'll mark both as "type_evaluation_report"? Let me think: revision 1 added DN50 and DN150, so second report covers extension tests — that's part of type evaluation too. I'll use "type_evaluation_report" for both. Hmm, but the schema role options include test_report. I'll go: NMi-2652375-01 → type_evaluation_report; NMi-3725759-01 → type_evaluation_report. Fine.

Documentation file: no. T12567-2 — "The construction of the measuring instrument is recorded in the Documentation folder no. T12567-2." That's a documentation_file test report entry: id "T12567-2", role "documentation_file". No date/pages. Include with id and role only.

Revision history:
- revision "Initial", date 12 June 2025, changes "Initial release."
- revision "1", date 6 July 2026, changes "Addition of DN50 and DN150, and software update."

Footnotes: The software table note "(*) The checksum is stated as a hexadecimal value." — marker "*", text. Include.

Date issued: 6 July 2026 (from issuing authority signature date; also revision 1 date). ISO format? The schema just says date_issued. I'll use "2026-07-06".

Scheme A → certificate.scheme: "A".

certificate.number: "R 49/2013-A-NL1-25.02" with revision noted; maybe include revision in revision field? Certificate number: "R 49/2013-A-NL1-25.02". I could add "revision": 1? Schema doesn't list revision at certificate level; revision_history covers it. I'll set number: "R 49/2013-A-NL1-25.02".

Now build model_level arrays.

Models:
- model_id "DN50", label "DN50/2”"? The markdown uses DN50/2”. I'll set model_id "DN50" and label "DN50/2\"" — careful with quote escaping. Use "DN50/2 inch"? Simpler: model_id: "DN50/2\"", ... JSON escaping fine. Actually to keep clean, model_id "DN50" with attributes... labels: I'll include label: "DN50/2\"". Hmm, the inch mark in markdown is ” (right double quote). I'll use label "DN50/2\"" with escaped quote.

Model-level characteristics:

attribute "nominal_diameter" values: DN50: 50, DN80: 80, DN100: 100, DN150: 150, unit mm.
attribute "minimum_flow_q1": 0.1, 0.25, 0.4, 1.0, unit m³/h.
attribute "transitional_flow_q2": 0.16, 0.4, 0.64, 1.6, unit m³/h.

attribute "verification_scale_interval": DN50 0.0001; DN80/DN100/DN150 0.001, unit m³.

Values structure per schema example: {"model": ..., "value": ...} — the strict structured-value shape applies to characteristics values; the model_level example in the rules shows {"model": "G1.6", "value": 2.5} without unit_symbol/footnote_markers per value — unit at attribute level. I'll follow the R137 example: values[] entries with model and value only (plus footnote_markers if needed).

Type-level characteristics list:

- measuring_principle: {value: "Electromagnetic", unit_symbol: null, unit_id: null}
- accuracy_class: {value: 2}
- environmental_class: {value: "M1 / O"}
- environmental_class_note? I'll include value "M1 / O (installed outdoors)" — parentheses in value ok? The "(installed outdoors)" is descriptive. I'll keep full string to not lose info. Actually environmental classes M1/O — O? R49 environmental... whatever, keep as-is.
- electromagnetic_environment: "E1"
- ambient_temperature_range: {min: -25, max: 55}, °C
- water_temperature_class: "T50"
- water_temperature_range: {min: 0.1, max: 50}, °C — from "T50 (+0,1 °C / +50 °C)". Yes.
- maximum_admissible_pressure: 1.6, MPa
- maximum_admissible_pressure_bar? I'll add "maximum_admissible_pressure" only. Hmm — but the 16 bar is in source. I could add separate key "maximum_admissible_pressure_alt": value 16 unit bar. That label is awkward. Alternatively value: "1.6 MPa (16 bar)" string — violates numeric preference. I'll include two characteristics: maximum_admissible_pressure (MPa) and skip bar? Information loss minor but acceptable. Actually, I could add "maximum_admissible_pressure" {value: 1.6, unit MPa} and note bar in... no. Let me add both with distinct labels: "maximum_admissible_pressure": 1.6 MPa; "maximum_admissible_pressure_bar_equivalent"? Too fabricated. Decision: include only MPa. Hmm, actually 16 bar is directly stated — not fabricated. I'll add "maximum_admissible_pressure" with unit "MPa" value 1.6, and second characteristic "maximum_admissible_pressure" can't duplicate. Use "maximum_admissible_pressure_max" no. Fine — I'll include "maximum_admissible_pressure": {value: 1.6, unit_symbol: "MPa"} and "maximum_admissible_pressure_bar": {value: 16, unit_symbol: "bar"}. It's a bit redundant but faithful. Eh... I'll do it.

Actually cleaner alternative: maximum_admissible_pressure: {value: {min:1.6,max:1.6}} no. Keep as decided.

- orientation: "All positions (horizontal, vertical or diagonal)"
- flow_profile_sensitivity_class: "U0 / D0" plus straightness condition. I'll do flow_profile_sensitivity_class: {value: "U0 / D0"} and straight_run_requirement: {value: "0 x DN upstream and 0 x DN downstream"}. Hmm "0 x DN" — string. OK.
- reverse_flow: {value: "Reverse flow measured; recorded on separate volume totalization with separate pulse output"}
- pressure_loss_class: {value: "Δp 16"}

- Also note constraints on flow rate selection? That's a note; could go into description or omit. I'll add to matrix table description for Table 3.

Footnote markers: Table 2 CRC has "(*)" footnote. Add footnotes: [{marker: "*", text: "The checksum is stated as a hexadecimal value."}]. And crc values get footnote_markers ["*"]? The rule 7 says when a value references a footnote record marker. The (*) is on column header. I can add footnote_markers to crc values. In matrix_tables rows, footnotes[] array at table level. I'll add footnotes to the software matrix table and mention marker in description.

columns: ["meter_size", "diameter_inlet_outlet", "q1", "q2", "q3", "q4", "ratio_q3_q1"]
